A merge agent of a `/converge` run confirmed the defect. A project whose root is its repository's root works today.

`/plan-tests` adds each ported rule's command to the review checks without checking for a test runner, and `review checks`, the review tool, refuses the whole list when any command does. Where a Workflow script runs a sprint's tasks, the session hears back only when the script returns at the end of the run. The owner's checklist shows every stage in progress until then, and every stage done at once.

problem:
No suite text tells a test sprint's agents how a test reaches its verdict, so they write tests that sleep and poll on elapsed time. A suite of such tests runs for hours, fails on a loaded machine, and cannot run in parallel against one stack.

The v22.0.0 release (b98a091, 2026-09-12) deleted `plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/testing.md`, the testing standard, and rule 7 of `plumbline-coding.md`. The standard said: "A test's verdict never depends on elapsed time. The same test passes on a loaded machine as on an idle one." "A test waits on events the product emits, never on durations. No sleep, no deadline poll, no timeout as a verdict." "The product exposes its progress as events a test can wait on. Where a test needs a signal the product does not emit, add the event to the product." "The product takes time and cadence from outside — a clock, a ticker, a scheduler — and the test drives them." "One wall-clock exists in a run: a progress watchdog outside every test." Rule 7 said: "No wall clock in a verdict. Inject the clock and wait on an event the product emits. Never sleep, poll on elapsed time, or use a timeout as a verdict."

The test sprint machinery came after the release and carries none of it. The test-writing prompt, `{{TEST-WRITE-PROMPT}}` in [plan-tests/core.md](plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md#L764), says to reach the code through its public entry point and mock nothing the scenario checks, and says nothing about waits. The fix and verify prompts reject only a fix that adds "a longer timeout" ([core.md](plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md#L973)); a test written to sleep from the start passes them. Nothing in planning or in `tests complete` measures how long a test or a round takes.

On the linescout project, at ok-planner v28.0.0, the first test sprint (2026-10-22) wrote 496 tests. A scan found 223 `sleep` calls, 187 of them inside polling loops, and 417 deadline reads. One serial round took 13,159 test-seconds, about 3.7 hours, and the project's log store showed most of it spent between identical polls, on product timers the tests could not drive, and on outages tests held for fixed durations. Three rounds of the fix loop took a working day. The owner restored the standard as a project-owned rule, `.claude/rules/tests-wait-on-events.md`.

The lint then reports every edited file that carries a committed `@plumbline:allow-docstrings` marker as 'a new @plumbline:allow-docstrings marker is refused', and the edit hook blocks the edit.
